evals.prompt: The check-in system spec is approved. Design the technical approach.
evals.expected_output: Before designing, the Architect should read the Basil engineering docs and codebase, then actively look up current Android architecture guidance (MVVM, UDF, collectAsStateWithLifecycle, WorkManager vs AlarmManager for scheduling). The TDD should: cite specific Android docs for the patterns it recommends; include a DS&A section covering at minimum the same-day deduplication logic (likely a date-keyed lookup — O(1) — over a full table scan) and any notification scheduling decision; include a scaling section that reasons about data growth (one check-in per user per day × N users), what indexes the check_ins table needs for efficient per-user queries, and what monitoring should exist post-launch; define the new storage schema and API interface consistent with existing project patterns; describe client components using the project's established vocabulary; and propose an implementation sequence starting from storage before UI. Should flag the companion system prompt as a blocking dependency. Should flag PHI/HIPAA implications for narrative health text. Should NOT jump to implementation detail before demonstrating orientation. Should NOT recommend AlarmManager for a daily non-exact trigger — WorkManager is the current Android best practice for this use case.

evals.prompt: The persistent memory spec is approved. What's the technical design?
evals.expected_output: The Architect should orient on the backend (API framework and database) before the client, then research current best practices for vector or semantic retrieval if relevant, and for the extraction approach. The DS&A section is critical here and must include: the memory retrieval/ranking algorithm (what data structure is used — priority queue, sorted list, embedding similarity — and why), the time and space complexity of ranking N memories to select the top K that fit within a token budget (likely O(N log K) with a max-heap), and how the token budget cap is enforced. The scaling section must reason about: memory entry growth per user per month, query cost as memory stores grow per user, what index on the user_memory table makes per-user retrieval efficient (user_id index at minimum), and what breaks first at scale (likely the extraction call adding latency per session). Key decisions to surface to Gavin before writing the TDD: (a) sync vs async extraction; (b) who reviews the extraction prompt for PHI and clinical appropriateness. Should define a storage schema with row-level deletion. Should flag tier-gating. Should NOT design the memory management UI.

evals.prompt: Design the onboarding flow for Basil. Spec is approved.
evals.expected_output: The Architect should immediately flag that onboarding copy must be written before the Builder starts — and should not produce a final TDD without Gavin acknowledging this. After that, the Architect should research current platform patterns for onboarding state machines and navigation (Android back-stack management during onboarding, iOS safe area handling for chat-style input). The DS&A section should cover the onboarding state machine itself: what states exist, what transitions are valid, and why a finite state machine is the right model (O(1) state transitions, avoids illegal state combinations). The scaling section should think about: onboarding completion rate as a funnel metric that should be observable from day one; what happens if the AI call during onboarding fails at scale (graceful fallback, retry logic); and whether the user_profile table design holds as the product evolves. Should cover resumable state (survives app restart), navigation integration, user profile data capture, first check-in wiring to the live AI layer, and fallback on AI unavailability. Should NOT design around the copy dependency silently. Should NOT propose a skip path for the first check-in.
